title: Ukraine's Military Has Less Access to Starlink
summary:
Ukraine's military has lost some access to Starlink, Ukrainian officials say. Starlink is a satellite internet system that Ukraine has used during its war with Russia.

Starlink is run by Elon Musk's company SpaceX. It uses more than 11,000 satellites that circle close to Earth. A safer military version is called Starshield.

It is not clear why the limits started. On Wednesday, Musk wrote on X that Starshield is owned and controlled by the U.S. government. He said any limits would have been ordered by the U.S. military and the president. The U.S. government had not answered yet, CBC News reported.

An adviser to Ukraine's president said the limits included a speed limit on Starlink equipment on drones. Ukraine uses the network for drones, air defense and supplies.

Experts say Starlink helps soldiers talk with faraway leaders, and it is very hard for enemies to block.
why_it_matters: It shows how internet from space has become very important, even helping a country stay connected during a war.

keywords.explanation: A satellite is a machine in space that circles Earth and sends signals.
The military is a country's army and other armed forces.
Drones are flying machines controlled from far away, with no pilot on board.
Air defense is the work of protecting an area from attacks from the sky.
To block a signal means to stop it from getting through.

background_read: Starlink sends internet signals from many satellites in space to dishes on the ground.
Because it works from space, it can help people connect where phone lines are broken, such as in a war zone.
Russia and Ukraine have been at war, and Ukraine's military has used Starlink to stay in touch.
